  • screening from neighbors and increase security.

questions.question: What are the advantages of air layering ?
questions.solution_html:
• ➢ High Success Rate for Difficult Plants: Effective for plants that rarely root from cuttings, such as mangos
  • lychees, and various ornamentals.
  • ➢ Faster Maturity & Large Size: Produces large, established plants quickly, often allowing them to bear fruit
  • or flowers much earlier than plants grown from seeds or cuttings.
  • ➢ Low Risk to Parent Plant: The new plant remains attached to the parent for nourishment until its own root
  • system develops, minimizing risk and stress to both.
  • ➢ Genetic Fidelity: The new plant is a clone, ensuring it has identical characteristics, such as fruit quality
  • growth habit, and color
  • ➢ .Simple & Low Infrastructure: Does not require greenhouse conditions, misting systems, or high humidity
  • environments to be successful.
  • ➢ Ideal for Rejuvenation: Perfect for propagating leggy or overgrown indoor plants like rubber plants or
  • dieffenbachia, allowing you to create a new, compact plant while resetting the original.
  • ➢ Works on Large Branches: Allows for the propagation of large, woody branches that would be impossible
  • to root through traditional cuttings

questions.question: Differentiate between simplicity and unity in landscape design?
questions.solution_html:
• Simplicity in Landscape Design - Omitting unnecessary elements that do not add to the overall design, fostering a
  • clean, organized, and uncluttered look.
  • Application
  • ➢ Limiting Varieties: Using fewer species of plants, but planting them in larger groups.
  • ➢ Restrained Palette: Restricting the color palette and materials (e.g., using only one type of stone for paths
  • and walls).Functionality: Focusing on essential design elements to avoid confusing, "fussy" landscapes.
  • Unity in Landscape Design
  • The "thread" that ties all components together, ensuring that different elements harmonize to create a complete
  • picture.
  • Application
  • ➢ Repetition: Repeating the same plant types, colors, shapes, or materials throughout the landscape to create
  • rhythm.
  • ➢ Interconnection: Ensuring that different areas of the landscape (e.g., lawn and patio) flow together
  • naturally
  • ➢ Style Consistency: Matching the garden style to the architecture of the home.
questions.final_answer: ➢ Style Consistency: Matching the garden style to the architecture of the home

  • growth habit, and color

  • to root through traditional cuttings
